title: BI Dashboard Extensions Platform Competitive Landscape

scope.description: Software vendors that compete for the same customers and jobs as an ecosystem extensions business modeled on Infotopics | Apps for Tableau: BI platform leads, dashboard creators and finance/planning teams at large organisations that want Excel-like tables, governed write-back, KPI and chart visuals, scheduled report distribution and dashboard guidance inside Tableau, Power BI or Looker Studio, with an on-premises option for security-sensitive enterprises. Infotopics | Apps for Tableau itself is the modeled subject of this domain and is therefore not listed as a player.
inclusionLogic: dedicated write-back specialists for Tableau that sell governed data-entry, forecasting and commenting extensions with on-premises or cloud editions (the head-to-head alternative to WriteBackExtreme and InputTables in a Tableau customer's evaluation)
premium viz-extension studios that sell chart-type and KPI extensions through the Tableau Exchange and compete with ShowMeMore, PowerKPIs and the visual storytelling products for the same creators

Power BI planning, write-back and financial-reporting visual vendors that meet the same products (SuperTables, InputTables, WriteBackExtreme, PowerKPIs) on the Power BI side, where the modeled company has ported its core extensions since 2022
Qlik Sense extension suites that are the structural twin of the modeled business on a third BI platform and set the benchmark for what an extension vendor looks like inside a larger software group
report-distribution, alerting and analytics-portal products that compete with MailScheduler, DashboardGuide and DashboardUsage for the adoption and delivery budget of a BI platform owner

the BI platform vendors themselves (Salesforce Tableau, Microsoft Power BI) whose native tables, viz extensions, Pulse/Copilot, subscriptions and Power Apps write-back are the substitute every extension purchase is measured against, and who own the marketplaces through which the extensions are distributed
notes: Business stats are only included when they were found on official company websites, about pages, newsrooms and press releases, official parent-company or investor-relations pages, official Tableau Exchange or Microsoft AppSource listings, or official LinkedIn company profiles (company-size bands); each stat preserves the company's reported scope and period.

Vendors report very different scopes (daily active users of free visuals, paying organisations, parent-group customers, LinkedIn headcount bands, platform-level revenue) that are not directly comparable with one another or with the modeled company's own figures (600+ organisations, 150+ countries, 30+ extensions, 32 partners, about 30 employees); scope labels make the asymmetry explicit rather than normalizing it away.

Several players sit inside larger software groups or have recently changed hands (Vizlib acquired by insightsoftware in August 2023, Acterys acquired by Vena Solutions in March 2026, Lumel in a first-party alliance with Microsoft for Planning in Fabric, Tableau inside Salesforce); group-level figures are labeled with the group scope.

Platform vendors do not disclose product-level Tableau or Power BI revenue or customer counts; the closest official metrics (Salesforce Agentforce & Data 360 ARR, Microsoft paid Fabric customers) are reported as such. Tableau Exchange publishes no official listing total, so the marketplace is described qualitatively inside the Tableau entry.

Checked but excluded: USEReady (its 2021 Writeback Extension for Tableau is no longer marketed on its site or the Tableau Exchange, its packaged product is Pixel Perfect paginated reporting, and it is a listed Apps for Tableau partner), DataBlick (a boutique Tableau consultancy whose extension work is open-source and demo-only) and Power ON (now sold as insightsoftware Visual Planner and covered under the insightsoftware entry).

players.name: Write-Back
players.description: Write-Back is the closest like-for-like rival to WriteBackExtreme: a dedicated write-back vendor that spun out of the Portuguese consultancy Xpand IT and sells a Tableau dashboard extension (plus a Power BI custom visual) for selecting marks, editing fields in a form and persisting the result to the customer's database, aimed at forecasting, planning, commenting and approval use cases. It ships three editions on the Tableau Exchange: Write-Back Server (on-premises, audit of all data and configuration actions, integrated authentication, multiple back-end databases, priced from $4,500 per year for up to 50 active users), Write-Back Cloud (vendor-hosted SaaS with a 30-day trial) and Write-Back Free (writes to a Google Sheet). Its published per-user price bands and dual Tableau + Power BI coverage contrast with WriteBackExtreme's Enterprise-only, on-premises-installer positioning.

players.name: M2 Form Builder
players.description: Form Builder from M2. technology & project consulting GmbH is a DACH-market write-back alternative: a browser-based editor for composing input forms from pre-built elements and embedding them in Tableau dashboards, running parameterised SQL against JDBC databases (Snowflake, Oracle, SAP HANA, PostgreSQL, SQL Server, DB2, MySQL) in the context of the dashboard, with CSS theming and configurable access restrictions. It is offered on-premises, cloud-hosted or as SaaS, listed on the Tableau Exchange and bundled into the M2 Tableau Toolbox on AWS Marketplace. It is more flexible than WriteBackExtreme on free-form SQL and form styling but lighter on governance (no published audit trail, approval workflow or enterprise licence tier), and it is a side-product of a roughly 45-person Berlin consultancy rather than a product company.

players.name: LaDataViz
players.description: LaDataViz is a two-person studio led by Tableau Visionary Tristan Guillevin and DataDev Ambassador Jessica Bautista that sells 21+ Tableau Viz Extensions (Sankey, Waterfall, Network, Radar, Chord, Beeswarm, Gauge, Polar Area and more), the BANg KPI-dashboard generator and a Figma-to-Tableau plugin, alongside free tools such as Filter Manager and Theme Generator. Free tiers are hosted by Tableau on the Tableau Exchange and paid licences are sold through its own store as one-off bundles, with all rendering in the browser and no data stored. It competes directly with ShowMeMore, PowerKPIs and EasyDesigns for the creator audience, on a low-price, community-led, indie model rather than the enterprise subscription and on-premises deployment the modeled company sells.

players.name: Lumel (Inforiver)
players.description: Lumel Technologies is the largest pure-play vendor of the Power BI equivalents of the modeled company's core products: the Inforiver family of custom visuals (Writeback Matrix for planning, forecasting and data entry; Reporting Matrix for financial statements, paginated and IBCS variance reports; Premium Table with 1,000+ columns; Analytics+ charts; Super Filter; EDITable master-data management) plus Inforiver Enterprise for server-side write-back workflows. In March 2026 it entered a first-party alliance with Microsoft to deliver Planning in Fabric IQ, metered in Fabric capacity units. It meets SuperTables, InputTables and WriteBackExtreme head-on on the Power BI side with a much larger team and an EPM/planning roadmap, but it is Power BI and Fabric only, leaving Tableau and Looker Studio to the multi-platform extension vendors.

players.name: Zebra BI
players.description: Zebra BI d.d. sells IBCS-certified, Microsoft-certified financial visuals for Power BI (Zebra BI Tables, Charts and Cards) and add-ins for Excel and PowerPoint, plus the newer Zebra AI dashboard generator, all aimed at P&L, variance and management reporting. A free limited tier on Microsoft AppSource feeds a very large user funnel that converts to Pro and Enterprise subscriptions. It competes with SuperTables, FinanceTables and PowerKPIs on the better-financial-tables-and-KPIs job in Power BI, but it is read-only reporting without write-back or planning and is Microsoft-stack only; its brand-led IBCS positioning and 1.5 million daily users show how far a single-platform visuals vendor can scale on freemium.

players.name: Acterys (Vena Solutions)
players.description: Acterys (legal entity Managility Pty Ltd, acquired by Toronto-based Vena Solutions in March 2026) is a Power BI and Excel planning, write-back and financial-consolidation platform: the Acterys Matrix and Visual Planning custom visuals provide governed data entry inside Power BI, the Modeller and Excel add-in handle multidimensional modelling, and pre-built connectors cover Xero, QuickBooks, HubSpot and Dynamics. It has the closest functional overlap with WriteBackExtreme and InputTables on Power BI but packages write-back as a full FP&A/xP&A suite sold to finance, now under a larger EPM vendor; Power BI and Excel only, with no Tableau or Looker Studio coverage.

players.name: Vizlib (insightsoftware)
players.hq: London, United Kingdom (parent: Raleigh, North Carolina, United States)
players.description: Vizlib is the structural twin of the modeled company on the Qlik Sense platform: founded in London in 2016 and acquired by insightsoftware in August 2023, it sells Vizlib Library (40+ chart types), Vizlib Collaboration (comments, governed write-back tables and input forms with approval workflows), Vizlib Finance Report (P&L, balance sheet, consolidations), Self-Service and User Portal extensions. Under insightsoftware, which also sells the Power ON-derived Visual Planner for Power BI, it is packaged into an Office-of-the-CFO portfolio with 32,000+ customer organisations. It does not touch Tableau, Power BI or Looker Studio and offers no scheduled filtered distribution comparable to MailScheduler, but it defines what an extension vendor looks like once absorbed into a large software group.

players.name: Curator by InterWorks
players.description: Curator (formerly Portals for Tableau, renamed in 2020) is the productised analytics portal of InterWorks, Tableau's inaugural Gold Partner: a white-labelled, role-based portal that unifies dashboards from Tableau, Power BI, Sigma and ThoughtSpot, adds embedded analytics, forms and write-back, scheduled report delivery and SSO, and is sold as Curator SaaS or Curator Custom together with consulting. It competes around the dashboard rather than inside it, overlapping MailScheduler, DashboardGuide and WriteBackExtreme on adoption, delivery and data-entry jobs, and its consultancy backing (about 275 people, 12 offices) plus multi-BI reach is the wedge against an extension vendor.

players.name: Metric Insights
players.description: Metric Insights, the originator of Push Intelligence for Tableau, sells a tool-agnostic BI and AI portal for BI platform owners: a governed catalog of certified dashboards and KPIs across Tableau, Power BI, Qlik, Sigma and 50+ other tools, BI Optimizer for retiring unused content, Distribution & Alerting with KPI alerts, personalised digests and scheduled bursts of pre-filtered content to email, Slack, Microsoft Teams and mobile, and an AI Concierge for conversational discovery. It overlaps MailScheduler most directly on scheduled, per-user filtered distribution and DashboardUsage on usage-based governance, but as a standalone portal it does not compete for in-dashboard table or write-back extensions.

players.name: Tableau (Salesforce)
players.description: Tableau is the platform the modeled company builds on, and its own roadmap steadily absorbs extension-vendor value: Viz Extensions (GA in 2024.2 with 30 viz types at launch, a native Table viz extension in 2024.3, Trusted Extensions in 2025.3) compete with SuperTables-style tables and ShowMeMore charts; Tableau Pulse, subscriptions and data-driven alerts substitute for MailScheduler and PowerKPIs; and Tableau Next / Agentforce agentic analytics on Data 360 move insight-to-action workflows into the platform, eroding the write-back niche. Tableau also owns the Tableau Exchange, the marketplace of accelerators, dashboard extensions, viz extensions and connectors through which every third-party extension is listed, safelisted and labelled trusted, so it controls the modeled company's primary distribution channel as well as its runtime.

players.name: Microsoft Power BI
players.description: Power BI, now part of Microsoft Fabric, is the rival platform whose native stack bundles much of what the modeled company sells as add-ons: the Power Apps visual embeds a canvas app in a report for write-back, Copilot for Power BI provides AI summaries and report generation, email subscriptions ship scheduled PDF and PowerPoint snapshots with dynamic per-recipient filtering, paginated reports cover pixel-perfect tables, and Microsoft AppSource distributes certified custom visuals. For a buyer choosing between Tableau plus premium extensions and Power BI plus Fabric, Microsoft's bundling is the platform-level substitute, while native limits (the Power Apps visual passes at most 1,000 records, needs separate Power Apps licensing and is unsupported in subscriptions; Copilot requires paid Fabric capacity) leave room for the Power BI editions of SuperTables, InputTables and WriteBackExtreme.
